chapter: Early music and the Olympia band
title: First music she remembers: Sonny Swan, Pete Fountain, Lizzie Miles
summary: She recalls piano player Sonny Swan and radio clarinetists, mentions Lizzie Miles and Willie Humphrey playing with her husband, and James Williams.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up with radio, records and family listening

blocks.x: Well, now, uh, I wanted to ask you about, uh, in your own life, what's the first music you remember? Either singing or a band playing or piano or what have you?

Well, uh, we used to have, uh, piano playing. We had, uh, we had a fellow who used to play piano, go all over with us. His name was, uh, Sonny Swarm. Oh, I've heard of him. He used to play piano, you know. I have a lot of them blues. I know him when I hear him, because I heard, I hear him every once in a while, I hear him on that little radio we have. And, uh, this fellow there that's gone to California, I think, or somewhere, uh, from that great clarinet player from here. Luzanne knew him good from when she was waking up town. Oh. And he plays a lot of the pieces that, uh, we used to hear. He's a great musician. Luzanne, Luzanne, what's his name again? The clarinet player. Who's name? From around magazine. How I used to know. The fellow, no, but comes on the radio. We went to Chicago or New York or something. I know him. Yeah, the part up there, the musician, the clarinet player, you see. Not Pete Fountain.
Pete Fountain. Yeah, uh-huh. Pete Fountain.
We didn't get your name down.
He wants your name, you know, on there.
So the secretary, I don't know whose voice is which. Luzanne.
No. Give all of this. He'll get that out.
He'll get that out. He played a lot of the tunes you said. Pete Fountain plays a lot of the tunes that you heard in those days, huh? Yeah. And he plays plenty of them pieces.

We had a lot of them pieces he plays, you know. That was a great number. Well, Lizzie Miles sings that all the time, that song, Bill Bailey, Won't You Please Come Home. She always gets on the radio, on the television, you know, if you're seeing that. She was another one who played with, you know, sang with all of them, Lizzie Miles. And this, yeah, he played with your daddy too. What do you call this other fella? Humphrey.

And the old man, you know, their daddy and all that. He all played together. Yeah. And see, we had so many of the pieces. Now this, what they call him? Not Johnny Sincere, another musician that played with James Williams. He was an old musician. He had the Armist brass band with, with, how long was it? Yes. He was a ball baller, James Williams. He was a trumpet player. He played with all them, he'd do them with some of his men. I've heard of him. He was from around Benito Street. He used to hang around James Williams. Yeah. That's what it was, around there. They'd hang around there.
